passages.scripture: What then shall we say that Abraham, our forefather, has discovered?

lines.text: Abraham is our forefather.
Abraham lived as a man on earth.
Abraham lived before us.
What did Abraham discover?
What can we say about what Abraham found?

passages.scripture: If Abraham was indeed justified by works, he had something to boast about, but not before God.

lines.text: How was Abraham justified?
Was Abraham justified only by his works?
If someone could be justified by only their works, then they could boast in their works.
If Abraham was justified only by works, then Abraham could boast.
But, Abraham has nothing to boast about before God.
In fact, none of us can boast before God.
In fact, none of us can boast before God that our works justify us.

passages.scripture: For what does the Scripture say? “Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness.”

lines.text: The Scripture speaks about Abraham.
Abraham believed God.
God counted Abraham’s faith as righteousness.

passages.scripture: Now the wages of the worker are not credited as a gift, but as an obligation.

lines.text: A worker receives wages.
The employer does not give wages as a gift.
The worker has a right to receive wages.
The worker deserves wages.
The employer pays wages because the worker is owed wages.
The employer is obligated to pay.
Wages are an obligation, not a favor.

passages.scripture: However, to the one who does not work, but believes in Him who justifies the wicked, his faith is credited as righteousness.

lines.text: A person may be wicked.
This person does not have enough good works to be counted righteous.
But God justifies the wicked.
This wicked person believes in God.
This wicked person has faith.
And God credits this person's faith as righteousness.

passages.scripture: And David speaks likewise of the blessedness of the man to whom God credits righteousness apart from works: “Blessed are they whose lawless acts are forgiven, whose sins are covered.

lines.text: There is a person who lacks good works.
God credits this person righteousness.
This man is blessed.
The righteousness that comes from God is far better than any righteousness that a sinner practices.
And the blessing that comes from God's righteousness is far better than any blessing that depends only on the works of a sinner.
David was a king and a prophet in Israel.
David speaks about this blessedness that comes from God's righteousness.
David says, “Blessed are those whose lawless acts God has forgiven.”
David says, “Blessed are those whose sins God has covered.”
If someone has done lawless acts, but God forgave them, then they are blessed.
If someone has sins, but the love of God has covered their sins, then they are blessed.

passages.scripture: Blessed is the man whose sin the Lord will never count against him.”

lines.text: Suppose a man has sinned.
If the Lord will not count this man's sin against him, then he is blessed.

passages.scripture: Is this blessing only on the circumcised, or also on the uncircumcised? We have been saying that Abraham’s faith was credited to him as righteousness.

lines.text: Paul asks a question about blessing.
Paul asks if this blessing is only for those who are circumcised.
Paul asks if this blessing is for the uncircumcised, as well.
Paul reminds us about Abraham.
Abraham believed God.
God counted Abraham’s faith as righteousness.

passages.scripture: In what context was it credited? Was it after his circumcision, or before? It was not after, but before.

lines.text: God credited righteousness to Abraham.
God credited righteousness to Abraham through faith.
God credited righteousness to Abraham before Abraham was circumcised.
God did not credit righteousness after Abraham was circumcised.
God credited righteousness to Abraham while Abraham was still uncircumcised.

passages.scripture: And he received the sign of circumcision as a seal of the righteousness that he had by faith while he was still uncircumcised. So then, he is the father of all who believe but are not circumcised, in order that righteousness might be credited to them.

lines.text: Abraham received circumcision as a sign.
Circumcision was a seal.
This circumcision seal showed the righteousness that Abraham had by faith.
Abraham had his faith before he was circumcised.
Abraham had his faith when he was still uncircumcised.
Abraham became the father of all who believe who are not circumcised.
God credits righteousness to these believers also.
God credits righteousness to the circumcised and to the uncircumcised.

passages.scripture: And he is also the father of the circumcised who not only are circumcised, but who also walk in the footsteps of the faith that our father Abraham had before he was circumcised.

lines.text: Abraham is our father.
Abraham is the father of those who are circumcised.
Abraham is not only the father of those who are circumcised.
Abraham is also the father of those who follow his faith.
These people walk in the footsteps of Abraham’s faith.
Abraham had this faith before he was circumcised.

passages.scripture: For the promise to Abraham and his offspring that he would be heir of the world was not given through the law, but through the righteousness that comes by faith.

lines.text: God gave Abraham a promise.
God also gave this promise to Abraham’s descendants.
God said Abraham would inherit the world.
God did not give this promise through the law.
God gave this promise through righteousness.
This righteousness comes by faith.

passages.scripture: For if those who live by the law are heirs, faith is useless and the promise is worthless, because the law brings wrath. And where there is no law, there is no transgression.

lines.text: If we could become heirs by living by the law then faith is useless.
If we could become heirs by living by the law then God’s promise is worthless.
This is because the law brings wrath.
Where there is no law, there is no breaking of the law.
If there are no laws, then there is no law to be broken.

passages.scripture: Therefore, the promise comes by faith, so that it may rest on grace and may be guaranteed to all Abraham’s offspring—not only to those who are of the law, but also to those who are of the faith of Abraham. He is the father of us all.

lines.text: God gave Abraham a promise.
This promise comes by faith.
God gives this promise by grace.
This promise rests on grace.
So this promise is certain to all the offspring of Abraham.
This promise is not only for those who follow the law.
This promise is also for those who have faith like Abraham.
Abraham is the father of us all.

passages.scripture: As it is written: “I have made you a father of many nations.” He is our father in the presence of God, in whom he believed, the God who gives life to the dead and calls into being what does not yet exist.

lines.text: God spoke to Abraham.
God said to Abraham, “I have made you a father of many nations.”
Abraham is our father.
Abraham is in the presence of God.
Abraham stands before God.
Abraham believed in God.
God gives life to the dead.
God calls things that do not exist into existence.

passages.scripture: Against all hope, Abraham in hope believed and so became the father of many nations, just as he had been told, “So shall your offspring be.”

lines.text: God promised Abraham that Abraham would be a father.
However, for a long time, it seemed hopeless that Abraham would be a father.
Fatherhood seemed hopeless because Abraham had no children, even when he was old.
And it seemed hopeless because his wife was old, too.
And it seemed hopeless because his wife had never birthed a child even when she was younger.
Abraham faced a situation that seemed hopeless.
But Abraham still chose to hope.
Abraham believed God.
God had told Abraham, “So shall your offspring be.”
Abraham believed the promise of God.
Abraham believed the promise of God that Abraham would have offspring and be a father.
Because Abraham believed, he became the father of many nations.

passages.scripture: Without weakening in his faith, he acknowledged the decrepitness of his body (since he was about a hundred years old) and the lifelessness of Sarah’s womb.

lines.text: Abraham was about one hundred years old.
Abraham saw that his own body was as good as dead.
Abraham saw that Sarah’s womb was lifeless.
However, Abraham did not weaken in his faith.
Abraham acknowledged these things.
And yet, Abraham still believed the promise of God.

passages.scripture: Yet he did not waver through disbelief in the promise of God, but was strengthened in his faith and gave glory to God, being fully persuaded that God was able to do what He had promised.

lines.text: Abraham heard the promise of God.
Abraham believed the promise of God.
Abraham did not doubt God’s promise.
Abraham did not let unbelief weaken him.
Abraham became strong in his faith.
Abraham gave glory to God.
Abraham was completely persuaded in his faith.
Abraham knew God could do what God had promised.

passages.scripture: This is why “it was credited to him as righteousness.”

lines.text: God counted Abraham’s faith as righteousness.
God credited righteousness to Abraham because of his faith.

passages.scripture: Now the words “it was credited to him” were written not only for Abraham, but also for us, to whom righteousness will be credited—for us who believe in Him who raised Jesus our Lord from the dead.

lines.text: Righteousness was credited to Abraham by God because of the faith of Abraham.
Scripture says “It was credited to him.”
These words were not only written for Abraham.
These words are also written for us.
Scripture isn't written only for the people from long ago.
The words of Scripture were also written for us today to receive what God means.
God credited righteousness to Abraham because Abraham believed.
And God will credit righteousness to us, too, if we believe.
And not only us, but God will credit righteousness to all who believe in Him.
God raised Jesus, our Lord, from the dead.
We believe in Jesus.
God will count us as righteous because of our faith.

passages.scripture: He was delivered over to death for our trespasses and was raised to life for our justification.

lines.text: Jesus was delivered over to death.
Jesus died because of our trespasses.
God raised Jesus to life.
God raised Jesus to life so we could be justified.
